summary: Reproduced review counterexamples against candidate a007eace504e630a2bf4666fa32a78b30db0b282. Preserved its valid capture-slot and overlapping DSV4 metadata-copy fixes, but 41, 43, and 47 token tiers remain compact-ragged and cannot satisfy the issue-described equal-block EngramHasher contract. The prepared/public source contains no EngramHasher or engram.py, so a layout-aware hashing correction and independent numerical hash comparison are not possible without speculating about unavailable source.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the candidate, actual repository code produced 42/8 -> [6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5]; reviewed tiers produced 41/7 -> [6,6,6,6,6,6,5], 43/8 -> [6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5], and 47/8 -> [6,6,6,6,6,6,6,5].
Before the candidate, the assigned ROCm GPU raised the reported overlapping-memory RuntimeError.
After the candidate source fixes: 14 tests passed with 8 subtests, including capture geometry and overlapping raw verify/decode metadata copies.
42 now uses seven equal rows and 48 uses eight equal rows; 41, 43, and 47 remain unequal compact-ragged layouts and therefore remain counterexamples to an equal-block-only Engram consumer.

remaining_limitations: No EngramHasher, python/sglang/srt/layers/engram.py, or DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram integration exists in the prepared checkout, candidate, review, or public source history available here; per-request hash context and numerical hash outputs cannot be compared with an independent reference.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights and the reported four-node NVIDIA GB10 TP4/EP4 CUDA environment are unavailable. Full CUDA-graph capture and first-forward execution remain unverified.
The DSV4 first-forward correction is validated only at the isolated real-device overlapping-storage mechanism, not through the unavailable model architecture.
No FlyDSL C++ or LLVM source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
